title: 第1198章 路标第1197章 边荒的站台
lines: 壳轨铺到第四片碎片时，卡拉斯停了手。这片碎片比前三片都薄，边缘极脆极透极轻，光丝缠上去时它轻轻一颤，颤完没有稳住，反而往虚空深处滑了一丝。不是丝不够紧，是这片碎片本身太轻，壳片和光丝的重量压上去，它承不住。
他用手指按住碎片边缘，茧印贴着极薄极脆极透极轻的碎片表面，碎片在他指尖下轻轻抖着。它在这里飘了太久，从来没承过任何重量，忽然让它当锚点，它站不住。
拼碎片的人蹲在旁边，光丝从指尖探出去贴着碎片边缘。它说这片碎片是膜层最早脱落的那一批，飘得最远，磨得最薄。在边荒飘了太久，边缘已经磨得和虚空一样薄了，让它当锚点，它会碎。
卡拉斯把壳片从碎片上拿起来。碎片卸了重，慢慢弹回来，但还在轻轻抖着。它被压了这么短的时间就已经站不稳了。他见过类似的抖——阿卡刚学端碗时爪子在碗沿上也是这么抖的。不敢用力怕夹碎，不敢太轻怕滑脱。
那时候阿卡端的是藤芽，现在这片碎片要承的是壳轨。他不再把壳片直接压在碎片上，而是将壳片放在两片碎片之间，让碎片从两侧夹住壳片。不是让一片碎片承所有重量，是让两片碎片分担。
两片碎片从两侧轻轻夹住壳片，壳片被固定住了，每片碎片只承一半的重量。光丝绕着壳片边缘缠了一圈，丝和纹路咬在一起，壳片稳稳地悬在两片碎片之间。
拼碎片的人看着壳片被两片碎片夹住，光丝在它背后轻轻飘着。它以前绑碎片都是一片绑一片，从来没想过让两片碎片分担重量。
它总是用光丝把碎片绑在自己身上，所有重量全由自己承，丝断了就再加一根丝，丝再断再加，加到后来自己也被压得走不动路，它就蹲在原地，把重量全压在脚底那片碎片上，那片碎片被压出了极细极细极细的裂纹。
它从来没跟谁说过这件事。卡拉斯看着它胸口那片最薄最透最亮的碎片，告诉它以后不用自己承全部重量，壳轨能把重量分给两片碎片，也可以分给更多碎片。路不是一个人扛的，是一段一段分着承的。
他把第三片壳片放在第五片碎片旁边。这一次不是用两片碎片夹，是把壳片平放在碎片面上，让碎片从下方托住壳片。碎片轻轻往上一顶，壳片被托住了。
它承重的方式和两片碎片夹不同——夹是分担，托是承接。碎片在下方极轻极轻极轻地托着壳片，每托住一丝重量就轻轻震一下，震完更稳了一分。
它在边荒飘了太久，从来不知道自己能承东西。现在有人把它放在壳片下面，它托住了，托得极稳极静极柔极透极韧极古极老极沉极闷极未知。
壳轨从第一碎片的光痕边缘一路铺过来，铺了很长一段。每一段壳片的放法都不一样——有些被两片碎片夹着，有些被碎片从下方托着，有些是光丝缠在碎片边缘悬空挂着。
边荒的碎片没有两片是完全相同的重量和形状，每一片碎片能承多重、该放在哪个位置，全得试。
拼碎片的人对碎片的了解帮了大忙——哪片碎片能承重，哪片碎片只能当路标不能压，它在边荒拼了太久太久太久，摸过每一片碎片的边缘。
卡拉斯负责铺壳片，它负责选碎片。选好了，卡拉斯把壳片放上去，它的光丝缠上去固定。两个人一个放一个缠，壳轨从第一碎片边缘铺到边荒更深处，每隔一段距离就有一片壳片在轻轻明灭。
卡拉斯把手里的最后一片壳片放在两片碎片之间。这是壳轨的第一段终点，前方碎片更稀更薄更脆更轻更散更杂更乱更混沌，暂时铺不过去。
他把壳片压了压，碎片从两侧轻轻夹住，光丝缠紧。这个位置离雾团收回第四缕雾丝的地方很近，离那个封着东西的碎片还有一段距离，壳轨暂时只能铺到这里。等壳轨更稳、收集的碎片更多、锚点分布得更密，再继续往深处铺。
拼碎片的人站在壳轨尽头，光丝在它背后轻轻飘着。它看着壳轨从第一碎片边缘延伸到自己脚下，它以前走几步丝就断，断了就得爬回去重新接。
现在壳轨铺通了，从这里到第一碎片，从第一碎片到边荒边缘，全有壳片在轻轻明灭。
它说它以前觉得边荒是没有路的地方，碎片飘了太久太久太久，从来没有什么东西能把它们连起来，自己用光丝绑了这么久也只是把自己绑住。
现在有了壳轨，碎片与碎片之间被壳片和光丝连在一起，边荒有了第一条路。这条路不是它一个人绑出来的——它负责选碎片，卡拉斯负责放壳片。
一个是拼碎片的人，一个是铺轨道的人，拼碎片和铺轨道原来是同一件事，都是把碎掉的、散掉的连起来。
卡拉斯把最后一片壳片压稳，把手掌覆在旁边那片碎片上。碎片轻轻一震。他会回来继续铺这段壳轨，等收集更多碎片，找到更多能当锚点的碎片，壳轨就能铺到更深处。
它现在已经是边荒的一部分了——有人选了它，把它放在壳片下面，它托住了壳片，壳片托着光丝。
它在这里飘了这么久，从今天起它不只是一片碎片，它是路的一部分。
content_en:
When the shell track reached the fourth fragment, Karas stopped. This fragment was thinner than the previous three pieces, and its edges were extremely brittle, translucent, and light. It trembled slightly when the light thread was wrapped around it. After trembling, it did not stabilize, but slipped deeper into the void. It’s not that the wire is not tight enough, it’s that the fragment itself is too light, and it cannot bear the weight of the shell and the light wire.
He pressed the edge of the fragment with his fingers, and the cocoon mark stuck to the surface of the extremely thin, brittle, transparent and light fragment, and the fragment shook gently under his fingertips. It had been floating here for too long, never bearing any weight, and suddenly it became an anchor and could no longer stand.
The person who was piecing together the fragments squatted beside him, with light strands sticking out from his fingertips and touching the edges of the fragments. It said that this piece of debris was the first batch of film to fall off, floated the farthest, and was worn the thinnest. It has been floating in the wilderness for too long, and the edges have been worn as thin as the void. If you let it be used as an anchor, it will break.
Karas lifted the shell pieces from the debris. The fragments were relieved of their weight and slowly bounced back, still shaking slightly. It was already unsteady after being pressed down for such a short time. He had seen similar tremors - Aka's paws trembled like this on the rim of the bowl when he first learned to hold it. Don't use too much force for fear of being crushed, don't be too gentle for fear of slipping.
At that time, Aka carried vine buds, but now this piece of debris has to carry shell rails. Instead of pressing the shell directly against the fragment, he placed the shell between two fragments, allowing the fragment to pinch the shell from both sides. Instead of having one piece bear all the weight, let two pieces share it.
The two fragments gently clamp the shell piece from both sides. The shell piece is fixed, and each fragment only bears half the weight. The light thread was wrapped around the edge of the shell, and the threads and lines were bitten together, and the shell was suspended steadily between the two fragments.
The person piecing together the fragments watched as the shell was sandwiched between the two fragments, with light threads floating gently behind it. It used to tie the pieces together one piece at a time, and never thought of letting the two pieces share the weight.
It always tied the fragments to its body with light wires, and all the weight was borne by itself. If the silk broke, it would add another silk, and if the silk broke again, it would add another. Finally, it was too heavy to walk, so it squatted in place, putting all its weight on the fragment under its feet, and the fragment was pressed into very fine, very fine cracks.
It never told anyone about it. Karas looked at the thinnest, most transparent and brightest fragment on its chest, and told it that it would not have to bear the entire weight in the future. The shell rails could distribute the weight to two fragments, or to more fragments. The road is not carried by one person, but is borne section by section.
He placed the third shell fragment next to the fifth fragment. This time, instead of using two pieces of fragment clamps, the shell piece is placed flat on the surface of the fragment, so that the fragment supports the shell piece from below. The fragments pushed upward slightly, and the shell pieces were supported.
Its load-bearing method is different from that of a two-piece fragment clip - the clip is to share the load, and the support is to bear it. The fragments below were very light, very light, very light, supporting the shell pieces. Every time they supported a little bit of weight, they vibrated slightly, and after the vibration, they became a little more stable.
It has been floating in the wilderness for so long that it never knew it could carry anything. Now someone put it under the shell, and it held it up, making it very stable, very quiet, very soft, very transparent, very tough, very ancient, very old, very heavy, very boring, and very unknown.
The shell track lay all the way from the edge of the light mark of the first fragment, covering a long distance. Each segment of the shell is placed in a different way - some are sandwiched between two fragments, some are supported by the fragments from below, and some have light threads wrapped around the edges of the fragments hanging in the air.
No two pieces of Bianhuang have exactly the same weight and shape. You have to try out how much each piece can bear and where it should be placed.
The person who pieced the pieces together helped a lot with their understanding of the pieces - which pieces could bear the load, which pieces could only be used as road signs and not be pressed down. It had been working together in the wilderness for too long, too long, and had touched the edges of every piece of debris.
Karas is responsible for laying out the shell slices, and it is responsible for selecting the fragments. Having chosen it, Callas placed the shell piece on top and wrapped its strands of light around it to hold it in place. Two people placed one on the other, and the shell track was laid from the edge of the first fragment to the deeper part of the wasteland. At intervals, a shell piece flickered and flickered.
Karas placed the last shell fragment in his hand between the two fragments. This is the end point of the first section of the shell track. The debris in front is thinner, thinner, brittle, lighter, scattered, messy, and chaotic, and it cannot be paved over for the time being.
He pressed the shell pieces, gently clamped the fragments from both sides, and wrapped the silk thread tightly. This position is very close to the place where the fog retracts the fourth wisp of fog. It is still some distance away from the fragment that seals the thing. The shell track can only be laid here for the time being. When the shell track becomes more stable, more debris is collected, and the anchor points are more densely distributed, then continue to lay deeper.
The person piecing together the pieces stood at the end of the shell rail, with light threads floating gently behind it. It watched the shell rail extend from the edge of the first fragment to its own feet. It used to take a few steps and the thread would break. If it broke, it would have to crawl back and reattach it.
Now that the shell track is paved, from here to the first fragment, from the first fragment to the edge of the wilderness, all the shell fragments are flickering.
It said that it used to think that the wilderness was a roadless place. The fragments had been floating for too long and for too long, and nothing could connect them. Even tying them with light threads for so long was just a way to tie them up.
Now that there are shell rails, and the fragments are connected by shell pieces and light filaments, there is the first road in the wilderness. It didn't build this road alone - it was responsible for selecting the fragments, and Karas was responsible for placing the shell fragments.
One is the person who puts together the pieces, and the other is the person who lays the tracks. Piecing the pieces and laying the tracks turns out to be the same thing, they are both connecting the broken and scattered things.
Karas pressed the last piece of shell firmly and placed his palm on the fragment next to it. The fragments shook slightly. He would come back and continue to lay this section of the shell track, and when he collected more fragments and found more fragments that could be used as anchor points, the shell track could be laid deeper.
It is now part of the wilderness - someone chose it and placed it under the shell. It supports the shell, and the shell supports the light filament.
